svg.aria-label: UART receive is a self-re-arming loop — and one error breaks it open

text.font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: UART receive is a self-re-arming loop — and one error breaks it open

text.font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Drive MCU (STM32G474, USART2 → ST-LINK VCP). The receive path only survives because each completed byte arms the next; an error exits that loop and nothing puts it back.

svg.text: HAL keeps receiving; these self-recover and need no callback. Only ORE and RTO abort.

svg.text: re-arms RX — the loop closes here

text.font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif
Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Losing a byte is fine — the parser resynchronises on the 0xB5DD sync word. Losing the RECEIVER is not: only a power cycle brings it back.

text.font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: Verified in stm32g4xx_hal_uart.c: FE/NE/PE are non-blocking, ORE/RTO call UART_EndRxTransfer() and then this callback.

text.font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: ORE could NOT be provoked from the host — a 128 kB flood at line rate never overran the ISR. Realistic sources are on-board: a long

text.font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif

svg.text: higher-priority ISR, a critical section, or motor EMI on the cable once the drivers are live. The fix is insurance, not a repair.

text.font-family: Helvetica Neue, Helvetica, Arial, system-ui, sans-serif
